description: Fingerprinting explores the science of identification: its history, civil and criminal uses, friction ridges and pattern types, taking a set of prints, and careers in biometrics.

versions.label: Checked against official scouting.org excerpts (partial verification)

provenance.notes: Requirement numbering and topics were checked against excerpts of official Scouting America pages (scouting.org) returned by a search index on 2026-10-24. The pages themselves could not be opened from the build environment, so wording was not compared word for word and some sub-items may be summarized from partial excerpts. Summaries are ScoutPath's own words. Requirement 2 appears to cover identification systems and biometrics, but its text was not visible, so it is not outlined yet.

references.label: Official merit badge page (scouting.org Merit Badge Hub)

requirements.summary: A short history of fingerprinting and civil versus criminal identification.

requirements.title: The science
requirements.summary: Where friction ridges are found, the principles of fingerprint science and positive identification.

requirements.title: Taking prints
requirements.summary: Making rolled and plain impressions on an identification card and recording prints with tape.

requirements.summary: The three basic fingerprint patterns and their subcategories, using your own hand.

requirements.title: Careers
requirements.summary: Careers in biometrics or fingerprinting and researching one of them.
